label: Sizun Jiang
narrative: Jiang is the instrument operator on the record - the third author of the 2022 Progress in Aerospace Sciences paper and, at the time, a member of Nolan's Stanford laboratory working on multiplexed ion beam imaging. His inclusion is what makes the Council Bluffs analysis reproducible in principle: MIBI at 200 nanometre lateral resolution with five-nanometre depth increments is not a technique a lone enthusiast can wield, and the paper's central finding - incomplete mixing of the constituent metals with no isotopic anomaly - is an imaging result before it is an interpretive one. He has since moved into infectious-disease and cancer spatial-biology work at Beth Israel Deaconess/Harvard, which is the ordinary trajectory; the UAP paper sits in his record as a single, clearly methodological contribution.
